newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: BP analyst sees oil price easing as stocks rebuild.
newsitem.headline: BP analyst sees oil price easing as stocks rebuild.

text.p: Oil stocks that were run down in early 1996 have rebuilt or are rebuilding quickly -- which should help bring back international oil prices to a more stable long term trend, British Petroleum Senior Economist Peter Davies said.
"Price tightness could go away very quickly... but it depends a lot on the weather," Davies told reporters.
"And that's something economists, which only have a marginally better record than meteorologists, should never predict," Davies added.
Davies attributed the recent rise in oil prices to an increase in demand of 500,000 barrels per day used to rebuild oil stocks run down during the severe 1995/6 winter.
But "forward prices suggest that should not be a long term factor... Consumption growth is more or less being matched by production increases," he said.
World oil prices hit new post-Gulf War highs this week with benchmark Brent Crude futures touching $24.70.
